## Context / Problem

Nine real scanner integration tests skip when binaries are absent at `tests/unit/test_code_review_conflict_markers.py:97-158`, `test_code_review_public_exposure.py:109-151`, and `test_code_review_ws5.py:347-399`. Verified installs neither scanner although `infra/compose/Dockerfile.reviewbot:43-71` makes them runtime prerequisites.

## Approach

Create one checked-in scanner lock manifest consumed by the review-bot image and CI provisioning. Pin Semgrep and Gitleaks versions plus artifact hashes. Add a native-binary Make target that fails on missing/wrong binaries and runs the focused integration tests. Invoke it from a reusable parallel workflow used by mirror CI and the exact-patchset Gerrit lane, and include that job in `vote.needs`.

Do not build Docker, install OpenGrep, or add this target to normal `make lint`/default local tests.

## Scope

- scanner version manifest and review-bot Dockerfile
- provisioning helper and explicit Make target
- scanner integration tests
- reusable mirror/Gerrit workflow and Verified parity guard

## Testing

Prove missing binary, wrong version/hash, valid Semgrep rule, and valid Gitleaks secret/SARIF behavior. Exercise workflow wiring and `vote.needs` parity structurally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Semgrep and Gitleaks versions and downloadable artifact hashes are single-sourced and consumed by deployment plus CI.
- [ ] The explicit native-binary target fails for missing or wrong scanners and passes the nine real integration contracts.
- [ ] One parallel reusable lane serves mirror CI and exact Gerrit patchsets and is required by the Verified vote.
- [ ] OpenGrep, Docker-image builds, normal `make lint`, and default local tests remain outside scope.
- [ ] The lane's expected cold-run cost is documented as approximately 1.5-3 runner-minutes without extending the existing 22-23 minute critical path when capacity is available.
